applies_to: .claude/skills/survey-explainer-fold/SKILL.md (Overview point 2; Step 4 answer-format template + following note; checklist)
EF-PHYSICAL.on_behavior: The dedicated section must include the concept's PHYSICAL MEANING as a required element: the concrete mechanism in physical quantities -- what is superposed or summed, what interferes or cancels, what a reader would observe or measure -- not only the symbolic derivation, a restatement of the governing equation, or a limit/asymptote. When the concept is one of a dual/analogous family (e.g. coherence bandwidth / time / distance; delay / Doppler / angle spreads; the Bello functions), the physical picture must be drawn PARALLEL to its siblings so the mechanism reads the same way across them, and any single ingredient the concept adds over its siblings named explicitly. EF-MATHEXHIBIT.title: survey-explainer-fold: math exhibits are untagged $$ KaTeX, not ASCII art in a fence
applies_to: .claude/skills/survey-explainer-fold/SKILL.md (Overview point 2; Step 4 rule + answer-format template; Step 6 sweep; checklist; Cross-references worked instances)
EF-MATHEXHIBIT.on_behavior: An ANNOTATED EQUATION or stepped derivation in the dedicated section is written as REAL math in an UNTAGGED `$$...$$` display block -- \underbrace / \overbrace with \substack{} labels, \begin{aligned} for a stepped derivation -- never drawn as ASCII art in a fenced code block. Fences are reserved for genuinely NON-math verbatim content: pseudocode, program listings, ASCII plots / curve sketches. Omitting \tag{N} (not the fence) is what keeps the exhibit cascade-free; untagged display math is a first-class warning-level citizen (hundreds of such blocks exist across surveys/; lint-math check #9 is WARNING, never error). Each untagged block carries a one-line HTML comment recording why, so a later reader does not 'fix' the warning into a cross-file break. The two REAL reasons not to tag: (1) SEMANTIC -- an exhibit re-displaying an existing equation must not mint a rival number for it; (2) CROSS-FILE -- equation numbers cited from outside the survey dir (wikis/) are unprotected, since propagate_xrefs only walks target_path.parent and XREF_FULL only matches the `[(N)](f.md#eq-N) <!-- xref:ID -->` form, while validate-refs checks that an anchor RESOLVES, never that the visible number MATCHES (todos/2026-07-09-crossfile-eq-number-fragility.md). Because Step 4 now mandates macros lint-math cannot validate (it checks delimiters statically and never runs KaTeX), Step 6 gains a MANDATORY `node viewer/tools/verify-katex-render.cjs FILE` render gate.
EF-MATHEXHIBIT.off_behavior: Pre-2026-07-09 behavior: Step 4 instructed 'Reproduce verbatim-sensitive math (program statements, annotated equations) as fenced code blocks, NOT as numbered $$ equations', justified by the claim that a new \tag would 'cascade every later equation number through the rest of the appendix'. That justification is FALSE for the in-file case -- renumber-equations.py Step 4 rewrites every in-file `<!-- ref:ID -->` link automatically and Step 6 propagates to survey-dir siblings, so an in-file cascade is a safe, routine, script-handled operation. The false rationale, plus a false dichotomy that never named the untagged-$$ third option, made ASCII art look mandatory: it produced the ╰──┬──╯ annotated Lagrangian in the G.8.6 worked instance, which the skill then generalized into a rule, which reproduced the defect in pusch-receiver sec 4.8.1 until the reader asked for KaTeX. No render gate in the sweep.

applies_to: .claude/skills/method-eval/SKILL.md (Step 1 Frame → Standing evaluation-hardening; Step 2 Stage-2/3 prompts) — carries the [opt:ME-INDEPENDENCE-AUDIT] site marker
ME-INDEPENDENCE-AUDIT.on_behavior: Before an oracle is trusted, list what it SHARES with the artifact under test — code paths, imported functions, and load-bearing ASSUMPTIONS (symmetry, Gaussianity, a scaling law). If the oracle shares the assumption being tested it is NOT independent and must be replaced or supplemented by a route sharing neither code nor that assumption. Stage 3 confirms the decisive oracle shares nothing with the failure mode. Rule: agreement between instruments that share a bug is not evidence.
ME-INDEPENDENCE-AUDIT.off_behavior: Pre-2026-07-11: independence is asserted ('a second agent re-derives from scratch') but the ORACLE's shared surface is unaudited, so a verifier can reuse the code-under-test's own arithmetic or its wrong premise — bug 2026-07-10-05 (three 'independent' MI computations all assumed the symmetry the quantizer bug broke) and the loop-reference that copied the implementation's indexing line (same bug).
ME-INDEPENDENCE-AUDIT.verified: 2026-07-11, the fading verification used a no-shared-code numerical oracle (rayleigh_fading_llr_density) that caught two high-SNR-limit constants + an inverted physical claim the analytic derivation missed (bug 2026-07-11-01)

ME-RED-ORACLE.title: method-eval: RED-first oracle (the oracle must FAIL on a deliberately-broken candidate before it is trusted to confirm)
applies_to: .claude/skills/method-eval/SKILL.md (Step 1 Frame → Standing evaluation-hardening; Step 2 Stage-2 prompt) — carries the [opt:ME-RED-ORACLE] site marker
ME-RED-ORACLE.on_behavior: Borrow TDD's iron law for the oracle itself: before the oracle/test is used to CONFIRM a candidate, run it on one deliberately-broken input and show it FAILS. An oracle never seen to reject is not known to discriminate; record the RED alongside the GREEN.
ME-RED-ORACLE.off_behavior: Pre-2026-07-11: the oracle is written and run on the real candidate only, so a check that CANNOT fail passes forever — bug 2026-07-10-03 (a gate whose bound admitted the bug) and bug 2026-07-10-05 (a loop-reference sharing the implementation's bug); neither was ever shown to reject a wrong input.
ME-RED-ORACLE.verified: 2026-07-11, verification-before-completion red-green precedent; the fading oracle's exponential-vs-Gaussian discrimination (R^2 1.0 vs 0.95) is the RED/GREEN in practice

RIS-EVAL-INDEPENDENCE.title: reference-implementation-study: evaluation-independence sub-pass (extend G0's derivation-independence into Phases 3 & 5)
applies_to: .claude/skills/reference-implementation-study/phases/phase-3-baseline.md (Evaluation-independence sub-pass) — carries the [opt:RIS-EVAL-INDEPENDENCE] site marker
.claude/skills/reference-implementation-study/phases/phase-5-precision.md (Evaluation-independence sub-pass) — carries the [opt:RIS-EVAL-INDEPENDENCE] site marker
RIS-EVAL-INDEPENDENCE.on_behavior: RIS's G0 gate (RIS-DERIV) makes the DERIVATION independent; this extends the same discipline to EVALUATION. In Phase 3 (baseline) and Phase 5 (precision), each load-bearing number gets a no-shared-code adversarial sub-pass: (1) re-verify it with an oracle sharing neither code nor the assumption under test (ME-INDEPENDENCE-AUDIT); (2) run the degenerate-case test — name the trivial solution that would satisfy the metric and confirm the metric REJECTS it (ME-ADVERSARIAL-METRIC). A metric that rewards triviality, or a number confirmed only by an oracle built from the same code/assumption, FAILS the sub-pass.
RIS-EVAL-INDEPENDENCE.off_behavior: Pre-2026-07-11: RIS independence stops at derivation (G0); the evaluation phases trust their own metric and an oracle that may share the implementation. Motivating case: a Phase-3 floor-limited-threshold baseline metric rewarded a trivial decoder (a large offset annihilating the messages) — caught late by hand, not by a gate.
RIS-EVAL-INDEPENDENCE.verified: 2026-07-11, sibling of RIS-DERIV; the method-eval fading verification demonstrated the evaluation-independence discipline end-to-end

RIS-PHASE0.title: reference-implementation-study: named Phase 0 (survey-side derivation authoring)
applies_to: .claude/skills/reference-implementation-study/SKILL.md (Phases table P0 row + the P0-vs-P1.5 note) -- carries the [opt:RIS-PHASE0] site marker
.claude/skills/reference-implementation-study/phases/phase-0-survey-derivation.md

P0 AUTHORS the foundation; the Phase-1.5 G0 gate (RIS-DERIV) INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVES it to attest soundness -- complementary, not redundant. Skip P0 when the survey already derives every operator the study implements.

A study introducing new load-bearing math authors it into the survey ad-hoc, inventing a study-local 'Phase 0' with no skill guidance for the deliverable (the procedure<->equation inventory + reduction-to-limit obligation), which recurred upstream twice (a decoder-parameter operator; a finite-precision recursion). SP-IMAGECITE.applies_to: .claude/skills/spec-provenance/SKILL.md (Phase 2 -- the draft-vs-current-spec gate) -- carries the [opt:SP-IMAGECITE] site marker
SP-IMAGECITE.on_behavior: When the current published artifact carries the value/formula only inside a figure, a rendered table image, or a screenshot that did not survive text extraction (blank line / garbled run), it cannot be text-read. The honest resolution is a fifth verification status, IMAGE-CITED: cite the exact clause/table, and verify our implementation by a bit-exact GOLDEN VECTOR (a spec test vector or a trusted reference implementation -- an official eval harness, a vendor reference kernel), NOT by transcribing the formula from memory and NOT by treating the value as text-verified. For a value TABULATED elsewhere in a readable table (e.g. an Annex reference-channel table giving the TBS), prefer that tabulated source and mark VERIFIED. Motivating: 2026-07-11 the conformance campaign ledger -- QAM constellation I/Q mapping (38.211 sec 5.1.3-5.1.6), DMRS comb k-formula (38.211 sec 7.4.1.1.2), TBS-procedure equations (38.214 sec 5.1.3.2) all extract blank; decisions 2026-07-03-01/-02 hit the same image-table class in 38.901.

Only the earlier ad-hoc 'image table -> cite, don't transcribe' (decision 2026-07-03) exists, without the golden-vector verification method named.
SP-IMAGECITE.verified: 2026-07-11, an upstream Phase-1 ledger (4 Sonnet extractors confirmed the three formulas blank in the .txt mirror; tabulated TBS used instead where available)

SP-LEDGER.title: spec-provenance: standing spec-provenance ledger artifact + per-spec version pin + cross-spec release-consistency
SP-LEDGER.applies_to: .claude/skills/spec-provenance/SKILL.md (Phase 4 -- Record and fix; Phase 0/2 version pin) -- carries the [opt:SP-LEDGER] site marker
SP-LEDGER.on_behavior: For a study touching many values across several artifacts, maintain a standing spec-provenance LEDGER -- one row per detail: {detail, value, source, VERSION/pin, section/table, verification method, status}. BG-RUNINBG.title: execution convention: durable background jobs use the tool's run_in_background, never nohup/& inside a foreground call
BG-RUNINBG.applies_to: .claude/rules/workflow.md (Diagram Rules — execution conventions, next to UTF8-WRITE) — carries the [opt:BG-RUNINBG] site marker
BG-RUNINBG.on_behavior: Launch any long-running job via the Bash/PowerShell tool's own `run_in_background: true`, NEVER via a trailing `&`, `nohup`, `setsid`, or `disown` inside a foreground tool call. A foreground tool call reaps its child processes on return, so a `&`/`nohup`-detached job is killed when the launching call completes (on WSL the distro also idles out and wipes /tmp). Durability is a launch-mechanism property, not `nohup`/`&` syntax. Corollary: design long-running drivers to flush+resume per unit of work (per-point/per-file) so an interrupted job relaunches at zero recompute. A PreToolUse advisory GATE that detects the anti-pattern at the moment of the call is the higher-reliability upgrade, held to a todo until its non-blocking surfacing contract is verified (todos/2026-07-12-background-launch-pretooluse-gate.md).
BG-RUNINBG.off_behavior: Pre-2026-07-12: no repo-wide convention; the nohup/& habit is re-attempted per long job and reaped, costing a relaunch (mitigated only where the driver happens to resume). Recurred N>=3 across sessions despite run_in_background being documented in the tool description — a habit-override failure a passive tool-description note did not prevent.
BG-RUNINBG.verified: 2026-07-12, mechanism is the tool's documented run_in_background primitive (used successfully for the fxp Phase-5 relaunch with per-point resume, zero recompute); recurrence grep across prompts/field-notes (2026-06-29, 2026-07-11, 2026-07-12)

UTF8-WRITE.title: tooling convention: file writes pass encoding='utf-8' (kill the recurring Windows GBK UnicodeEncodeError)
UTF8-WRITE.applies_to: .claude/rules/workflow.md (code conventions, near the determinism rule) -- carries the [opt:UTF8-WRITE] site marker
UTF8-WRITE.on_behavior: Any repo tool/script that does file I/O with possibly-non-ASCII content MUST pass encoding='utf-8'. WRITES -- Path.write_text(...), open(path,'w'), json.dump(obj, handle) -- and READS -- Path.read_text(), open(path), json.load(open(path)) -- both default to the platform locale code page, which on Windows is GBK/CP936: a WRITE raises UnicodeEncodeError and a READ raises UnicodeDecodeError the moment the content carries a non-ASCII glyph (minus-sign U+2212, times, superscript-2, em-dash, ~, box-drawing). For stdout, set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 or route non-ASCII to a file. Recurrence: bug 2026-06-22-01 (status-line GBK crash, fixed locally, convention not generalized), bug 2026-06-24-01 (emdash corruption), >=3 write repeats in the 2026-07-11 quantizer session, and a READ crash during THIS harvest (json.load(open('.claude/skill-options.json')) failed on the file's own em-dashes).
UTF8-WRITE.off_behavior: Pre-2026-07-11: no repo-wide convention; each tool re-learns the footgun -- a write with a non-ASCII glyph crashes under GBK on Windows and the fix is re-discovered per tool.
UTF8-WRITE.verified: 2026-07-11, empirically reproduced + fixed (analyze_quantizer_bler / comparison_matrix / bler_tables writers all set encoding='utf-8'); bug 2026-06-22-01 diagnosis (GBK/CP936 stdout)

RIS-REFPERF.title: reference-implementation-study: conformance studies establish REFERENCE PERFORMANCE and benchmark against it, not the raw requirement (Phase 1)
applies_to: .claude/skills/reference-implementation-study/phases/phase-1-scenario.md (Deliverables -> Reference performance bullet) -- carries the [opt:RIS-REFPERF] site marker
.claude/skills/reference-implementation-study/SKILL.md (Phases table, Phase-1 gate cell) -- carries the [opt:RIS-REFPERF] site marker
RIS-REFPERF.on_behavior: If the study's success criterion is an EXTERNALLY PUBLISHED NUMBER (a model card's reported accuracy, a leaderboard entry, a paper's headline pass@k), treat it as REFERENCE PERFORMANCE + a configuration stack (prompt template, few-shot k, decoding params, harness version, answer-extraction rule), NOT the receiver's target. In Phase 1, before computing any margin: (1) establish the underlying reference performance via the spec-provenance skill -- it lives in the WG contribution primary records (rungs 1-2), not the published spec -- and record it in the spec-provenance ledger (SP-LEDGER); (2) benchmark the sim against the REFERENCE, stating requirement = reference + margin explicitly. Escape (never silent): if the reference performance genuinely cannot be acquired, say so and benchmark against the requirement WITH the margin-stack caveat disclosed. Non-conformance studies (no external mandated target) skip this. Composes with spec-provenance (does not duplicate its primary record machinery); the report-side disclosure is SIM-REQBASIS.
RIS-REFPERF.off_behavior: Pre-2026-07-23: RIS Phase 1 names no reference-performance step. A study benchmarks against the PUBLISHED number directly, silently treating published-minus-measured as a capability delta -- so a margin that is mostly harness and prompt difference reads as merit. The failure is silent and survives every gate (the W4.2 '+5.33 dB MET' bug, caught only by owner intuition). The existing calibration-residuals check-4 (reconcile the metric basis) cannot even fire, because the reference performance was never acquired -- only one basis exists.
RIS-REFPERF.verified: 2026-07-23, an upstream post-mortem: the reference performance re-anchored the verdict off the published requirement onto reference + margin (upstream bug 2026-07-22, margin conflated with the margin stack)

SIM-REQBASIS.title: sim-report-completeness: a conformance report decomposes requirement = reference + margin and names which basis the verdict is measured against
SIM-REQBASIS.applies_to: .claude/rules/sim-report-completeness.md (Three emphases -> 'A conformance requirement is not a target') -- carries the [opt:SIM-REQBASIS] site marker
SIM-REQBASIS.on_behavior: When a sim/implementation report benchmarks against an external standardization conformance requirement, Section 2 states the decomposition requirement = reference + margin with the REFERENCE PERFORMANCE sourced to the WG contribution record (via spec-provenance; established in Phase 1 under RIS-REFPERF), and the verdict names WHICH BASIS it is measured against: a margin vs the reference is receiver headroom; a margin vs the requirement is mostly the margin stack and must NOT be cited as headroom. If the reference cannot be acquired, disclose that and benchmark against the requirement with the caveat (explicit n/a beats silent absence). Broader than RIS: applies to any sim report, including one not produced via the RIS workflow. This is calibration-residuals check 4 (metric-basis reconciliation) applied to the requirement itself. Prose discipline, NOT a check-report-completeness.py mechanical gate (not wired to the checker).
SIM-REQBASIS.off_behavior: Pre-2026-07-23: Section 2 grades per-parameter conformance (EXACT/IDEALIZED/...) but does not require decomposing the published number into reference + configuration delta, so a report can cite margin-vs-published as a capability gain without disclosing that most of it is harness difference (the '+5.33 dB MET' framing).
SIM-REQBASIS.verified: 2026-07-23, an upstream report re-anchored: its sections now decompose published = reference + configuration delta and cite the reference performance as the operating point

CR-SPLIT.title: calibration-residuals check 6: split the population + check rig preconditions before attributing a reproducible number
CR-SPLIT.on_behavior: Before stating what a measured quantity MEANS: (a) decompose an aggregate rate into sub-populations and confirm the effect survives in the one being attributed; (b) verify the measurement rig's own preconditions, especially on a deliberately 'easy'/control case; (c) establish seed/noise variance at one point before believing a trend across a swept variable. Corollary: judge a statistic against a MATCHED NOISE FLOOR (the same statistic under a change that alters nothing real), never against an absolute constant.
CR-SPLIT.off_behavior: Checks 1-5 only. A residual may be attributed from an aggregate statistic without population decomposition or rig-precondition verification, and gates may use absolute thresholds.
CR-SPLIT.earned_from: an upstream measurement session: five wrong attributions in one session, EVERY ONE attached to a number that reproduced exactly. Headline instances: a 96.54%/0.00% population split overturning a 'the codebook erases the population' finding by ~5x and changing its mechanism; a forced-AWGN control rig that was an identically null channel (silent for 28% of seeds) whose noise-only output was written up as a demapper property; a single-seed 'trend' that five seeds showed was monotone; and a z=+10.65 symmetry defect that moved a codebook no more than resampling did, against a threshold below the sampling-noise floor. Recurrence beyond this session: 12 prior field-notes match the wrong-attribution-on-a-reproducible-number pattern, incl. 2026-07-16-wave3-a4-green-gates-hiding-real-defects.
refs: an upstream derivation wiki (correction, retraction, gate resolution)

BG-GUARD.title: workflow.md BG-RUNINBG: PreToolUse gate blocks foreground-background Bash launches
applies_to: .claude/rules/workflow.md (BG-RUNINBG rule) -- carries the [opt:BG-GUARD] site marker
.claude/settings.json (hooks.PreToolUse[matcher=Bash])
.claude/hooks/guard-foreground-background.py
BG-GUARD.on_behavior: A PreToolUse hook inspects every foreground Bash call (run_in_background not true) and, if the command backgrounds a job via a trailing `&`, `nohup`, `setsid`, or `disown`, BLOCKS it (exit 2) with a message to relaunch via run_in_background:true. The OPERATIVE runtime toggle is the severity file `.claude/foreground-bg-severity` in {off | warn | error}: `error` blocks, `warn` is stderr-advisory only (does NOT prevent the reap), `off` disables. High-precision detector: `&&`, fd-redirects (2>&1, >&2), arithmetic bitwise-and ($((a & b))), and `&` inside quotes/comments are NOT flagged. Fails OPEN on any error; Bash-only (PowerShell `&` is the call operator).
BG-GUARD.off_behavior: Set `.claude/foreground-bg-severity` to `off`: no gate, and BG-RUNINBG relies on the documented rule alone -- the state that let the reap recur N>=6 across upstream sessions.
BG-GUARD.verified: 2026-07-21, 7 bad-pattern fixtures blocked + 13 good-pattern fixtures allowed (incl. &&, 2>&1, $((3&1)), quoted &, $#, comment-hidden &, & wait); production py-launcher path + malformed-input fail-open confirmed

ME-REAL-EXIT.title: method-eval: capture the REAL exit code (imported from verification-before-completion)
applies_to: .claude/skills/method-eval/SKILL.md (Step 1 Standing evaluation-hardening; Stage-2 RUN step) -- carries the [opt:ME-REAL-EXIT] site marker
ME-REAL-EXIT.on_behavior: Verification captures the process's REAL exit code, reported SEPARATELY from any pipe: `| tail`/`| head` masks it, and on PowerShell `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` and `2>&1` on a native exe fake success (the exit-code footgun the PowerShell tool rule already documents). ME-NO-DELEGATED-WAIT.title: method-eval: a verify/verdict agent returns its finding as TEXT, never a background-waiter stub
applies_to: .claude/skills/method-eval/SKILL.md (Step 1 Standing evaluation-hardening; Stage-3 verdict) -- carries the [opt:ME-NO-DELEGATED-WAIT] site marker
ME-NO-DELEGATED-WAIT.on_behavior: A verify/verdict agent must return its finding as TEXT in its own turn; it may NOT spawn background work (an MC script + a 'waiter') and return a 'still running... I'll be notified... waiting' stub. A stub is an empty result in disguise -- the pipeline's final return becomes a non-answer, and the Workflow journal's agents_empty_result=0 does not catch it.
ME-NO-DELEGATED-WAIT.off_behavior: Pre-2026-07-11: a Stage-3 independent-verify agent could spawn concurrent background scripts + a waiter and return a stub, so the substantive verdict silently came from Stage 2 and the independent-verify stage effectively did not complete (observed in wf_8029dd44-37e; caught only because the orchestrator did not trust the pipeline result and re-reproduced the falsification).

ME-FALSIFIER.title: method-eval: pre-registered falsifier per rubric criterion (criterion, oracle, falsifier triple)
applies_to: .claude/skills/method-eval/SKILL.md (Step 1 Standing evaluation-hardening; rubric) -- carries the [opt:ME-FALSIFIER] site marker
ME-FALSIFIER.on_behavior: Each viability criterion pre-registers its FALSIFIER -- the observation that would reject the candidate -- BEFORE the run, so a rubric criterion is a {criterion, oracle, falsifier} triple and the Stage-3 verdict states which falsifier fired (or that none did). CLAUDE.md '## Agent Fan-Out -- Sizing and Failure Diagnosis' -- names DRS-HARDEN as the encoded default
DRS-HARDEN.on_behavior: Evidence agents are sized and shaped so a per-agent iteration/tool-call cap death (~36-40 calls) is survivable: ~3-4 questions per agent, EXACT paths (no Glob discovery), WebFetch capped at <=2 in favour of WebSearch snippets + local-spec grep, and an incrementally-written _scratch/<id>.md file as the deliverable so a step-cap death still leaves evidence on disk. The orchestrator treats an empty-string return as agent death. Never rely on a terminal structured-output call as the only output -- its throw silently nulls inside parallel() and jumps a null-only retry.
DRS-HARDEN.off_behavior: `agent_hardening: off` in config/operational-scale.json restores the legacy schema-first deliverable, 5-question sizing, and unrestricted Glob/WebFetch (pre-2026-06-25). MATH-REDERIVE.title: Derivations: every new derivation gets one independent re-derivation before it lands
applies_to: .claude/rules/workflow.md -- Math Derivation Rules, carries the [opt:MATH-REDERIVE] site marker
surveys/**, wikis/**, reports/** -- any document adding or materially changing a numbered derivation
MATH-REDERIVE.on_behavior: Before a new or materially-changed numbered derivation is committed, ONE independent re-derivation is run by an agent that did not author it, deriving from first principles BEFORE reading the target text, and its findings are applied or explicitly rejected with a reason. The reviewer's raw output is preserved under the document's _scratch/. Sizing follows DRS-HARDEN: exact paths, no Glob, file-first incremental deliverable, under ~30 tool calls, kept on Opus because this is adversarial verification gating correctness.
MATH-REDERIVE.off_behavior: The author's own numerical checks are the only gate, as before.
MATH-REDERIVE.rationale: Measured upstream on one survey: four verifiers, ~10 minutes each, found 17 error-class defects in material that had ALREADY passed the author's numerical checks and one prior adversarial review -- two claims exactly backwards, a formula refuted by its own sanity anchor two sentences away, and a citation misattribution inside the paragraph about attributing correctly. Nothing else measured in that session approached the yield per unit effort. It also catches what a value-checking oracle structurally cannot: an oracle confirms arithmetic while the conclusion drawn from it is inverted. Oracles test values; re-derivation tests reasoning.

MATH-BASIS.title: Derivations: every quantity measurable on two bases declares which one, at the point of use
applies_to: .claude/rules/workflow.md -- Math Derivation Rules, carries the [opt:MATH-BASIS] site marker
surveys/**, wikis/**, reports/** -- any document stating a derived quantity
viewer/tools/check-basis-declarations.py -- the mechanical gate
MATH-BASIS.on_behavior: A quantity that can be measured on more than one basis carries its basis where it is first used and wherever it is compared: sample counts as per-channel or total; statistics as realised-population or ensemble; time constants as mean-error or mean-square; a variance by naming WHICH quantity's variance; a sign convention by naming the section that sets it; a dB figure as dBc, dBFS or dB-relative-to-named. Two values on different bases are never compared without a stated reconciliation.
MATH-BASIS.off_behavior: Bases are declared ad hoc, as .claude/rules/calibration-residuals.md check 4 already requires at the moment of ATTRIBUTION rather than of authoring.
MATH-BASIS.rationale: Measured upstream on one survey: metric-basis conflation was the LARGEST single defect class, 5 of 17 findings -- N per-channel vs total, sigma_F^2 vs a different scheme's variance, tau mean vs mean-square, sigma_eps realised vs ensemble, and a sign convention contradicting the section that set it 130 lines earlier. calibration-residuals check 4 already forbids exactly this, was loaded, and fired five times anyway: it owns the moment of attribution, and nothing owned the moment of authoring. Same structural gap [opt:PLAN-REDFIRST] was created to close.

SIM-BASELINE.title: sim-report-completeness: validate the CONTROL arm at its own best operating point before publishing a comparative margin
SIM-BASELINE.on_behavior: Before publishing a margin, state for the baseline what you would state for the candidate: its configuration, why that configuration, and evidence it is not being run below its own best setting. Cheapest sufficient check: vary the baseline's most-arbitrary knob and confirm the chosen setting is not dominated.
SIM-BASELINE.off_behavior: Report the comparative margin with the treatment arm alone carrying a configuration justification; the baseline's setting is taken as given.
SIM-BASELINE.rationale: A comparative result is a DIFFERENCE and is exactly as sensitive to the control as to the treatment, but scrutiny is never symmetric: the treatment is what is being proposed and gets the derivations and the adversarial review, while the control inherits an obvious-looking default nobody questions. Measured 2026-08-02 (bugs/2026-08-02-coded-phy-gain-measured-against-uncalibrated-baseline): a Coded-PHY gain published at +3.20 dB was +1.60 dB on a fair basis -- the discriminator baseline's raw soft LLR decoded WORSE than its own hard decisions, so roughly half the reported gain was the baseline's miscalibration rather than sequence detection. A handicapped control inflates the effect AND reproduces perfectly on every re-run, so repetition, seeding discipline and CI cannot surface it -- 40+ Monte Carlo runs did not. This is calibration-residuals check 6 applied at the moment a comparative margin is PUBLISHED rather than when a residual is attributed.
